newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on cool, wet forecast.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on cool, wet forecast.

text.p: Forecasts for a cool week in the U.S. Midwest, followed by a wet weekend sent new crop CBOT soybean futures spiralling lower for the second straight day, pit sources said.

Weather Services Corp said temperatures would be below normal on Tuesday with a gradual warm-up expected into the weekend. A storm system was predicted to produce 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain this weekend with 40 to 60 percent coverage for the Corn Belt, WSC said.
But some long-range outlooks suggested a shift to a wetter pattern, a scenario that would aid developing soybean crops.
Some meteorologists said a ridge of high pressure would move west this week, opening the door for more moisture to move into the central U.S. Midwest.
Soybeans ended 11-3/4 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower with November down 11-3/4 at $6.34-1/2. The November has shed roughly 25 cents per bushel in the last two days.

Agronomists said the soybean crop was not permanently damaged by the dry month of July but needed moisture as more of the crop entered the pod fill stage. USDA on Monday said 38 percent of the crop had reached that stage as of Sunday, compared with the five-year average of 33 percent.

"The corn plant and soybean plant are at a point in time where operation under moisture deficiency is not in their best interest," said Gary Pepper, agronomist with the University of Illinois in Champaign.
"In the soybeans, a number are blooming and a considerable number are working to produce pods," he said.
August escaped the brunt of the sell-off as no deliveries have been posted. CBOT on Tuesday said soybean registrations in the three deliverable points totalled 65,000 bushels.

Traders said the market shrugged off Sparks Companies' U.S. soybean production estimate of 2.686 billion bushels, saying it was nearly identical to USDA's outlook. USDA in July estimated production at 2.69 billion.
On the day, Refco Inc bought eight million bushels November and sold six million, Merrill Lynch bought three million November and Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold 1.5 million November, traders said.
Continental Grain spread 1.5 million August/September at 90 to 91 cents, premium August, and Tenco Inc spread one million November/August at $1.19 to $1.20, premium August.
In options, Rand Financial sold 300 November $6.25 puts at 24 cents, traders said.
Also, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 200 September $7.00 calls at 10 cents, sources said.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 26 percent, down from 28 percent on Monday.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 45,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 52,520. Options volume was pegged at 23,000 contracts, against Monday's 27,075.
